LESSON: WRITING 2.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you make your composition interesting to read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions
2. create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 2.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 2.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions

What this means
In this part you learn to identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes

What this means
In this part you learn to create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner. (skill: create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions.
3. Practise this skill: create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you make your composition interesting to read?
2. Why is it important to proofread your composition?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions.
5. Be able to: create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
